payload.project_context: KuaiRand-style implicit-feedback ranking; scarce official experiments; primary metric combines GAUC and nDCG@5; Windows/Linux compatible code

avoid_when: Only raw text, images, or very long sequences are available without structured context.
Feature IDs have excessive cardinality without hashing, frequency pruning, or an unknown bucket.
The official serving budget only permits linear models.
cards.summary: Build a strong dense baseline with categorical embeddings, explicit bounded-order feature crosses, and an MLP residual tower. Compare a compact DeepFM/DCNv2-style scorer against an embedding-plus-MLP baseline under an identical feature contract.
cards.title: Residual cross-feature ranker for implicit-feedback scoring
use_when: Most features are categorical IDs, buckets, or low-dimensional numeric context.
A reliable nonlinear interaction baseline is needed before trying sequential or transformer architectures.
GPU memory and inference latency permit embedding tables plus a small cross network.

avoid_when: Event ordering or timestamps are unreliable.
History construction cannot guarantee exclusion of the current impression and all future events.
The dataset has no reusable item metadata or interaction entities for aggregation.
required_features: historical interaction labels or engagement signals
cards.summary: Create strictly pre-impression user histories using several recency windows and aggregate prior exposure, click, watch, and engagement behavior by item, author, category, and global context. Include counts, smoothed rates, time-since-last-event, and recency-decayed aggregates.
cards.title: Causal multi-window behavior-history features
use_when: Timestamped interactions are available and user behavior changes over time.
The base ranker needs inexpensive sequential signal without a full sequence model.
Cold-start and sparse-history cases can be represented with explicit missing/history-length indicators.

avoid_when: Candidate groups are unavailable or grouping is reconstructed unreliably.
Labels are too noisy for pair construction and no stable pointwise baseline exists.
A listwise loss would create impractical batch-size, padding, or platform-memory costs.
required_features: impression or ranking-group identifier when available
sample weight or propensity-related field when justified
cards.summary: Start with weighted binary cross-entropy on logged impressions, then test a modest within-impression-list pairwise or LambdaRank-style auxiliary loss. Tune the auxiliary weight on validation GAUC and nDCG@5 rather than assuming pairwise optimization improves both.
cards.title: Pointwise ranking loss with list-aware auxiliary objective
use_when: Each impression group contains multiple displayed candidates or meaningful within-user candidate sets.
Positive labels are sparse and the model otherwise overfits easy negatives.
The training pipeline can form groups without mixing examples across timestamps or users incorrectly.

avoid_when: The benchmark supplies an immutable official validation split that must be used unchanged.
Chronological order is absent and no defensible time proxy exists.
Validation is so small that single-split selection must be replaced by repeated or blocked evaluation.
required_features: event timestamp or ordered split key
cards.summary: Use a chronologically later validation partition, fit all transforms only on training rows, and select checkpoints by the stated primary metric while recording both GAUC and nDCG@5. Fix seeds, save split manifests, and retain the best and final checkpoints to detect overtraining.
cards.title: Temporal validation and checkpoint-selection protocol
use_when: Official test labels are scarce or hidden and model choices must be made from local validation.
Behavior drift makes random-row validation overly optimistic.
Several architecture, feature, or loss variants need a comparable selection rule.

avoid_when: All categorical vocabularies are small, fixed, and fully observed in training.
Hash collisions cannot be tolerated for a business-critical identifier without a retained dictionary.
Useful fallback metadata and context are entirely unavailable.
required_features: categorical IDs with train-set frequency counts
item/context metadata or global-prior fallback features
cards.summary: Frequency-prune or hash rare categorical IDs, reserve explicit unknown buckets, regularize embeddings, and expose frequency and missingness indicators. Ensure unseen users or items fall back to metadata, context, and global priors instead of invalid indices or uncontrolled random embeddings.
cards.title: Sparse-ID regularization and cold-start fallback
use_when: User, item, author, or category vocabularies have long tails.
Validation or deployment-like test data contains unseen or infrequent entities.
Large embedding tables cause unstable rare-ID estimates or excessive memory use.

avoid_when: The task is exploratory and intentionally prioritizes diverse hypotheses over strict promotion gates.
No stable baseline, seed control, or resource measurement is available yet.
Metric noise is too high to support fine-grained comparisons from a single run.
cards.summary: Promote a change only when it improves the primary validation score across fixed seeds or temporal blocks without an unacceptable nDCG@5 regression, runtime increase, or memory increase. Add features and components incrementally, log deltas against one locked baseline, and reject gains that disappear under reruns.
cards.title: Cost-aware ablation and model-promotion rule
use_when: Official experiment opportunities are scarce and each submission needs strong evidence.
Many plausible feature, loss, and architecture changes compete for limited compute.
The final system must run consistently on both Windows and Linux.

system: You are a senior recommender-systems research curator. Plan practical, non-duplicative literature cards for an autonomous experiment judge. Cover architecture, feature, objective, training, evaluation, robustness, efficiency, and experimental-decision details as relevant. Prefer established methods and actionable configurations over broad surveys. Return one JSON object only.
